seoTitle: How to Close Your Google Workspace Account in 2026
metaDescription: Step-by-step guide to closing a Google Workspace account before your next billing cycle, avoiding future charges and account recovery issues.
intro: If you're no longer using your Google Workspace business email, closing the account properly stops future billing and avoids the confusion of an accidental renewal. This guide covers the full cancellation process and what to watch out for.

steps.heading: Access the Admin Console
steps.body: Sign in with your admin account and navigate to the billing section where your subscription details are listed.

steps.heading: Navigate to billing and cancellation options
steps.body: Find the option to cancel your subscription, which is typically located within the Billing settings.

steps.heading: Cancel the Workspace subscription
steps.body: Confirm the cancellation, noting the effective date so you know exactly when access and billing will stop.

steps.heading: Download or remove your data
steps.body: Before the account closes fully, download any important emails, files, or contacts you need to keep for your records.

steps.heading: Avoid automatic renewal and recovery issues
steps.body: Double-check the cancellation confirmation and mark your calendar for the billing cutoff date to make sure you're not charged again.

faq.question: Will I be charged again after canceling Google Workspace?
faq.answer: As long as the cancellation is confirmed before your next billing date, you shouldn't be charged for a new cycle.

faq.question: How do I make sure my domain and data are fully removed?
faq.answer: Follow through the full account closure process in the Admin Console, which includes removing domains and confirming data deletion.

faq.question: Can I still recover my account after closing it?
faq.answer: There's usually a limited recovery window after closure, but data and services aren't guaranteed to be restorable once fully deleted.

faq.question: Is closing the account the same as canceling the subscription?
faq.answer: Canceling stops billing, while fully closing the account also removes the domain and data — they're related but not identical steps.
